body_es: GitHub Actions es la plataforma de CI/CD integrada en GitHub que permite definir flujos de trabajo automatizados directamente en el repositorio como ficheros YAML dentro del directorio .github/workflows/. Un workflow se compone de events que lo desencadenan, jobs que se ejecutan (en paralelo por defecto) y steps dentro de cada job que se ejecutan en secuencia. Los events más comunes son push y pull_request, que pueden filtrarse por rama. Los jobs corren en runners, máquinas virtuales gestionadas por GitHub; ubuntu-latest es el más usado y el más económico. Cada step puede ser una acción reutilizable de la comunidad (uses: actions/checkout@v4) o un comando de shell directo (run: pytest tests/). Las variables de entorno se definen con env a nivel de workflow, job o step; los secretos se configuran en los ajustes del repositorio y se inyectan con la sintaxis ${{ secrets.NOMBRE }}. La acción actions/setup-python@v5 configura el intérprete de Python en el runner con la versión deseada. La caché de dependencias con actions/cache reduce significativamente los tiempos de ejecución al evitar descargar paquetes en cada run. Los artefactos, binarios o informes generados durante el pipeline, pueden guardarse con actions/upload-artifact para descargarlos después. Las matrices de estrategia permiten ejecutar el mismo job en varias versiones de Python o varios sistemas operativos simultáneamente. En el ejemplo se muestra un workflow completo que ejecuta los tests de un proyecto Python en cada push a main y en cada pull request.
body_en: GitHub Actions is the CI/CD platform built into GitHub that lets you define automated workflows as YAML files stored in the .github/workflows/ directory of your repository. A workflow consists of events that trigger it, jobs that run in parallel by default, and steps inside each job that run sequentially. The most common events are push and pull_request, which can be filtered by branch name. Jobs run on runners, virtual machines managed by GitHub; ubuntu-latest is the most widely used because it is fast and inexpensive. Each step is either a reusable community action referenced with uses, such as actions/checkout@v4, or a direct shell command written under run. Environment variables can be defined at the workflow, job, or step level using the env key; secrets are configured in repository settings and injected via the ${{ secrets.NAME }} expression syntax. The actions/setup-python action configures the Python interpreter on the runner at a specific version. Dependency caching with actions/cache cuts execution time dramatically by avoiding re-downloading packages on every run. Artifacts, binaries or test reports generated during the pipeline, can be uploaded with actions/upload-artifact and downloaded from the Actions UI. Build matrices let you run the same job across multiple Python versions or operating systems in parallel with a single workflow definition. The example shows a complete workflow that runs tests on every push to main and on every pull request targeting that branch.
example_code:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Run tests
        run: pytest tests/ -v --tb=short
